issues.t: Camshaft position sensor can melt and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic or rubber smell, smoke from under the hood and the check engine light on. Some cars stalled or wouldn't start, and several owners reported fires.
issues.why: The camshaft position sensor can overheat and melt, and the heat can spread to the cam cover and wiring harness and start a fire. Recalls 04V-357 and 04V-394 replace the sensor and add a fuse. Some owners said the sensor failed again after the fix.
issues.next: If you smell burning or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and get everyone out. Daewoo's US dealers closed soon after the recall, so many cars never got the fix. Call NHTSA's recall line with your VIN and have a shop check the sensor, fuse and wiring.

issues.t: Timing belt or tensioner fails and bends valves
issues.sym: The engine dies on the road, sometimes with all the warning lights on, and then cranks but won't start.
issues.why: The 2.2L engine uses a rubber timing belt, and the valves hit the pistons if it breaks. Owners reported belt failures between about 60,000 and 84,000 miles, some caused by a failed tensioner bearing or the belt rubbing the engine. Repairs often meant bent valves or a replacement engine.
issues.next: If you can't prove it was done, replace the belt, tensioner, idler pulleys and water pump now. Daewoo owners suggest about every 55,000 miles because the tensioner tends to fail first. If it has already broken, don't keep cranking; have it towed and tested before paying for repairs.

issues.t: Overheating, blown head gasket or coolant in the cylinders
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, steam or white smoke comes from the engine or exhaust, coolant disappears, the oil looks milky, or the engine shakes at start-up.
issues.why: Owners reported failed thermostats, blown head gaskets and coolant leaking into the cylinders, possibly from the intake manifold gasket. Adding cold water to a very hot engine cracked one owner's block.
issues.next: If the gauge rises, pull over and shut the engine off. Never open the radiator cap or pour cold water into a hot engine. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the oil checked for coolant before driving again.

issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out at speed or when stopping, sometimes over and over, and may not restart right away.
issues.why: Owners linked stalling to the failing camshaft sensor, fuel pump trouble, wiring faults and timing belt failure. Some problems came back after repairs.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have it scanned for codes and checked for the recall sensor, fuel pressure and timing belt condition.

issues.t: Check engine light stays on
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on and stays on or flickers, sometimes with slow acceleration. Some cars failed state inspection.
issues.why: Most owners traced the light to a failing camshaft position sensor. Others had loose gas caps or other sensor faults.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If it's the camshaft sensor, check whether the recall was done. A flashing light means a misfire, so have it checked right away.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips, won't shift or fails
issues.sym: The transmission slips, won't shift for several minutes, surges when shifting or fails completely. One owner's failed before 50,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners reported worn transmissions and failed shift solenoids, which are the electric valves that control shifting.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or won't shift, avoid hard driving and have a shop scan for transmission codes. A solenoid is a far smaller repair than a rebuild.

issues.t: Brakes wear quickly and rotors warp
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding, a shaking pedal or steering wheel when stopping, and pads and rotors that need replacing often. One owner needed four brake jobs in a year.
issues.why: Owners reported early pad wear and warped or rusted rotors that couldn't be resurfaced.
issues.next: Have the pads, rotors and calipers inspected. Replacing worn rotors instead of resurfacing them, and checking for a sticking caliper, usually helps.

issues.t: Brake pedal goes soft or sinks to the floor
issues.sym: The pedal feels soft or nearly reaches the floor, and the car takes longer to stop. One owner lost control and hit a median.
issues.why: The reports don't name one cause. A leak, air in the lines or a failing master cylinder are the usual reasons for a sinking pedal.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Don't drive if the pedal goes low. Check the brake fluid level and have the whole system inspected for leaks before driving again.

issues.t: ABS light on or front wheels lock when braking
issues.sym: The ABS light comes on, and the front wheels lock up or the brakes grab hard. Some owners reported crashes.
issues.why: Owners reported ABS problems and worn ABS wheel speed sensors. When the ABS is faulty, the wheels can lock in a hard stop.
issues.next: Brake gently and leave extra distance. Have the ABS codes read; a wheel speed sensor or its wiring is a common fix.

issues.t: Brake lights don't come on
issues.sym: The brake lights don't light when you press the pedal. Some owners also couldn't shift out of Park.
issues.why: A failing brake light switch at the pedal cuts the brake lights and the signal that releases the shift lock.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights. If they're out, get the switch replaced soon so drivers behind you can see you stopping.

issues.t: Airbag warning light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag light stays on all the time.
issues.why: The airbag system has stored a fault. One dealer said the airbag control module needed replacing; others couldn't find the cause.
issues.next: Assume the airbags may not work until it's fixed. Have a shop with an airbag-capable scan tool read the codes.

issues.t: Shifter sticks in Park or shift button breaks
issues.sym: The shifter won't come out of Park, won't go into gear unless you hold the lock button, or the shift button breaks off.
issues.why: Owners reported broken shift lever buttons and sticking shift linkage. A bad brake light switch can also keep the shifter locked in Park.
issues.next: Check that the brake lights work, since that often points to the switch. Have the shift lever and its lock checked and repaired.

issues.t: Key sticks in the ignition
issues.sym: The key won't turn to the lock position or won't come out, and in some cases the key gets hot.
issues.why: Owners reported sticking ignition lock cylinders and switches.
issues.next: Don't force the key. Have the ignition lock cylinder and switch checked, and check the shift lock, since the key can't come out unless the car is fully in Park.

issues.t: Headlights cut out or headlight housing overheats
issues.sym: The headlights go out at random while driving, sometimes along with power accessories and the horn, or a headlight assembly overheats and cracks.
issues.why: Owners reported electrical faults at the headlights and overheated headlight assemblies.
issues.next: Pull over safely if the lights go out. Have the headlight connectors, switch and wiring checked for heat damage.

issues.t: Exhaust or fuel smell inside the car
issues.sym: You smell fuel or exhaust inside the cabin, especially through the air vents, or hear a metal rattle from the muffler.
issues.why: Owners reported fumes in the cabin and rusted mufflers. Exhaust leaks can let carbon monoxide into the car.
issues.next: Open the windows and get it checked soon. Have the exhaust system and fuel lines inspected for leaks. Headaches or drowsiness while driving are a sign to stop driving the car.

issues.t: Car pulls to one side or steering rack fails
issues.sym: The car pulls left or right at any speed, or the steering feels loose or noisy.
issues.why: Owners reported a failed steering rack, worn suspension parts and alignment problems.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Have the steering rack, tie rods and front suspension inspected, then get an alignment.
issues.sevReason: Pull or worn rack; gradual. First step covers sudden heaviness.

issues.t: Hard starting or no-start
issues.sym: The engine needs many tries to start, cranks but won't start, or keeps blowing fuses.
issues.why: Owners found blown engine computer fuses, a smoking camshaft sensor that damaged the wiring, and weak electrical connections or grounds.
issues.next: Check the battery and fuses first. Have a shop check for spark and fuel and look over the cam and crank sensor wiring.

issues.t: Power windows stop working
issues.sym: A power window won't move, or one goes up by itself and then won't move.
issues.why: Owners reported failed window motors and switches.
issues.next: Have the switch and motor tested. Repair it before bad weather if the window is stuck down.

issues.t: Dashboard pad warps or separates
issues.sym: The dash top lifts or separates near the windshield, and air from the vents blows in the driver's face.
issues.why: Owners reported dashboard padding coming loose and warping.
issues.next: This is mostly cosmetic, but have it secured if it blocks the defroster or your view.

issues.t: Passenger-side A-pillar padding added (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The front passenger could suffer worse head injuries by hitting the pillar beside the windshield in a crash.
issues.why: The cars didn't meet the federal head-impact standard at the passenger-side windshield pillar. Recall 01V-180 adds padding to the pillar.
issues.next: Check the recall status with your VIN on NHTSA's site. If it isn't done, ask a shop whether the padding can still be installed.

issues.t: Seat belts won't retract or lock up
issues.sym: A seat belt locks while retracting or won't pull out or wind back in.
issues.why: Owners reported sticking seat belt retractors.
issues.next: A belt that doesn't work properly may not protect you in a crash. Have the retractor checked and replaced if needed.
